title: Code audit: Censor
description:
attached_molecule: ce-wisp-7d4l
attached_formula: mol-polecat-work
attached_at: 2026-05-08T06:07:10Z
dispatched_by: unknown

Full codebase audit of Censor. Goals: identify dead code, unused dependencies, convention drift, test coverage gaps, security surface issues, and structural problems. Use bd doctor --check=conventions, bd lint, and deep code reads. File child beads for any findings worth tracking.
notes:
Audit complete. Build: clean (116/116 tests pass). Findings:

COVERAGE GAPS:
1. test_storage.cpp is empty — CensorDb (8 methods) has zero test coverage. Active learning tests use :memory: db for insert/confirm/reject suggestion only.
2. analyze_stroke_weights() and detect_ceiling_grid() have zero test coverage — compiled into censor.so but never called from any test target (test_clustering only compiles feature_vector.cpp and spatial_clustering.cpp directly, not the histogram or grid prepass files).

CODE QUALITY:
3. Three duplicate cosine_similarity implementations: knn_classifier.cpp (KNNClassifier::cosine_similarity), active_learning.cpp (file-scope), discovery_queue.cpp (cosine_sim). All same algorithm, slight variations.
4. generate_uuid() in active_learning.cpp uses shared mutable static std::mt19937 — not thread-safe. store_suggestions() could be called from multiple threads.
5. std::gmtime() used in now_iso8601() in censor_db.cpp — not thread-safe (uses static buffer). CensorDb docs say 'caller must serialize' but fragile.

STRUCTURAL:
6. Four placeholder .cpp files: clustering.cpp, grid.cpp, storage.cpp, overlay.cpp — each is just a single-line comment.
7. CENSOR_API macro defined in cluster.h but used outside clustering (feature_vector.h, stroke_weight_histogram.h). Confusing location.
8. Mixed header guard styles: #pragma once in clustering/grid headers, #ifndef guards in classifier/storage/overlay headers.
9. ClusterBoundsEntry and HistogramBin lack default member initializers (= {}) unlike other structs.
10. sqlite3_close() in CensorDb::close()/destructor — sqlite3_close_v2() would be safer if prepared statements leak.
11. StrokeWeightBands::thresholds[8] — magic number 8 duplicated in struct def and loop guards without a named constant.

title: IClassifier interface + k-NN with cosine similarity
description: Two deliverables: (1) Define swappable IClassifier interface per SPEC-censor-core.md §6: predict(FeatureVector) → ClassifyResult { label, confidence 0-1, above_threshold }, add_example(FeatureVector, label, is_negative), label_counts() → map<string,int>. (2) Implement KNNClassifier: cosine similarity between query and all stored examples. k=KNN_K (constant, default 5). Weighted voting (closer neighbors = more weight). Confidence = fraction of k neighbors agreeing on winner. Per-class activation: predictions only when class has >= SEEDING_THRESHOLD_PER_CLASS (default 10) labeled examples. Open string labels, no enum. File: src/classifier/iclassifier.h, src/classifier/knn_classifier.cpp + .h. Depends on FeatureVector.
acceptance_criteria: IClassifier is a pure virtual interface. KNNClassifier passes 5+ tests: cosine similarity correct, weighted voting works, per-class activation threshold enforced, confidence calculation correct, empty classifier returns no prediction.

title: Grid system — spatial sampling mesh with lazy cell evaluation
description: Implement grid system per SPEC-censor-core.md §5. Page dimensions divided into approximate squares, count = GRID_DEFAULT_DIVISIONS (named constant, placeholder). Each cell is an independent training sample. Lazy evaluation: cells compute nothing until queried. Cell ↔ cluster mapping: given clusters from spatial_clustering, map which clusters overlap which cells. Cross-boundary clusters are whole (selection snaps to full cluster regardless of cell). User control: single slider adjusts division count (coarser ↔ finer), adjustable anytime (re-maps clusters). File: src/grid/grid_system.cpp + .h. Depends on Cluster struct.
acceptance_criteria: Grid divides page into cells. Lazy evaluation: no work until cell queried. Cluster-to-cell mapping correct including cross-boundary clusters. Slider changes division count and re-maps. 3+ unit tests.

title: Feature vector extraction — 12 dimensions per cluster
description: Implement 12-dimensional feature vector computation per cluster. Features per SPEC-censor-core.md §4: (1) total stroke length, (2) dominant orientation (angle, histogram of segment angles), (3) stroke weight mean, (4) stroke weight band (from histogram calibration), (5) closed loop count, (6) closed loop total area (shoelace), (7) connectivity to adjacent cells, (8) fill presence (bool→float), (9) aspect ratio, (10) bounding box area, (11) element count, (12) parallel offset distance (if two dominant parallel strokes, normalized distance, else 0). All normalization values as named constants with placeholder values — calibrated during seeding run. Deferred features (FFT periodicity, symmetry, termination) not in scope. File: src/clustering/feature_vector.cpp + .h. Depends on Cluster struct.
acceptance_criteria: FeatureVector struct holds 12 floats. Extraction function computes all 12 from a Cluster. Named constants defined with placeholder values. 3+ unit tests with synthetic clusters verify each feature dimension.

title: Fix thread-unsafe generate_uuid() in active_learning.cpp
description: generate_uuid() in active_learning.cpp uses shared mutable static variables: 'static std::mt19937 rng{std::random_device{}()}; static std::uniform_int_distribution<uint32_t> dist;'. std::mt19937 is not thread-safe. If store_suggestions() is called from multiple threads concurrently, there is a data race on the static RNG state. C++11 guarantees thread-safe initialization of static locals but not thread-safe access after initialization. Fix: use thread_local instead of static for the RNG (thread_local is per-thread, no synchronization needed), or protect with a mutex. The distribution object is stateless after construction so it can remain static. Note: store_suggestions() currently has no callers that run from worker threads but the BackgroundWorker design could enable this in future.

title: Extract cosine_similarity to shared math utility
description: Three separate implementations of cosine similarity exist: (1) KNNClassifier::cosine_similarity in knn_classifier.cpp (private static, checks na2==0||nb2==0), (2) file-scope cosine_similarity in active_learning.cpp (uses denom<1e-9f threshold, clamps to [0,1]), (3) cosine_sim in discovery_queue.cpp (checks na2==0||nb2==0, identical to #1). The implementations differ in their zero-vector guard (exact-zero check vs epsilon threshold) and clamping behavior. This is a DRY violation and risks divergence. Proposal: add a free function censor::cosine_similarity(const FeatureVector&, const FeatureVector&) to censor_types.h or a new src/math_utils.h (inline, no .cpp needed). Remove the three duplicates. The active_learning variant's epsilon guard (1e-9f) and [0,1] clamping are arguably more robust — use that as the canonical implementation.

title: Standardize header guard style (#pragma once vs #ifndef)
description: Headers use two inconsistent styles: #pragma once (newer, supported by all major compilers): cluster.h, spatial_clustering.h, stroke_weight_histogram.h, ceiling_grid_prepass.h, feature_vector.h, grid_system.h. #ifndef guards (traditional): censor_abi.h, censor_types.h, iclassifier.h, knn_classifier.h, active_learning.h, censor_db.h, background_worker.h, confidence_overlay.h, completeness.h, debug_viz_data.h, discovery_queue.h. Recommendation: standardize on #pragma once — simpler, no guard name collisions, all target compilers (GCC, Clang, MSVC) support it. Note: censor_abi.h is the public C header consumed by Rapida — it should keep traditional guards for maximum portability (pure C compatibility). All internal C++ headers can use #pragma once.

title: Use sqlite3_close_v2 in CensorDb::close() to handle statement leaks
description: CensorDb::close() calls sqlite3_close(db_) directly. If any sqlite3_stmt has been prepared but not finalized (e.g. due to an early return in an error path), sqlite3_close() returns SQLITE_BUSY and the handle is NOT closed, leaving db_ as a dangling pointer after 'db_ = nullptr'. The CensorDb destructor ignores the return value. sqlite3_close_v2() is the correct choice for RAII wrappers: it deregisters the handle immediately (even with open statements) and the handle is deallocated when the last prepared statement is finalized. This is standard SQLite RAII practice. Change both sqlite3_close calls in censor_db.cpp to sqlite3_close_v2.

title: Replace placeholder .cpp files with module registration comments
description: Four source files are single-line placeholder comments: src/clustering/clustering.cpp ('// clustering module — placeholder'), src/grid/grid.cpp ('// grid module — placeholder'), src/storage/storage.cpp ('// storage module — placeholder'), src/overlay/overlay.cpp ('// overlay module — placeholder'). These are included via GLOB_RECURSE and compile to empty translation units. The real implementations are in subdirectory files (spatial_clustering.cpp, grid_system.cpp, censor_db.cpp, etc.). The placeholders add noise. Two options: (A) delete them (GLOB_RECURSE still picks up the real files), or (B) convert to module-level doc comments listing what the module contains (useful as entry points for newcomers). Recommend option A since the CLAUDE.md already documents the module layout.

title: Add default member initializers to ClusterBoundsEntry and HistogramBin
description: ClusterBoundsEntry (debug_viz_data.h) and HistogramBin (debug_viz_data.h) lack default member initializers, unlike other structs in the codebase (Cluster, CensorOverlayEntry, FeatureVector etc. all have '= {}' or '= 0' defaults). ClusterBoundsEntry: 'int cluster_id;' and 'float bounds[4];' are uninitialized. HistogramBin: 'float low; float high; int count;' are all uninitialized. In current code, get_cluster_bounds() and compute_histogram() always fully initialize before use so there's no active bug, but it's inconsistent with the rest of the codebase and fragile. Fix: add '= {}' / '= 0' defaults to all members, consistent with how Cluster and CensorOverlayEntry are defined.

title: Move CENSOR_API macro out of cluster.h to a visibility header
description: CENSOR_API (for test-visible internal symbols) is defined in src/clustering/cluster.h but is used by feature_vector.h and stroke_weight_histogram.h which are not conceptually cluster-module files. The feature_vector.h comment 'include cluster.h /* CENSOR_API macro */' is a smell. The codebase now has three visibility macros: CENSOR_EXPORT (in censor_abi.h, for public DLL ABI), CENSOR_API (in cluster.h, for test-visible internals), and raw __attribute__((visibility(default))) sprinkled on KNNClassifier, CensorDb, BackgroundWorker, ActiveLearner, ConfidenceOverlay. Proposal: move CENSOR_API to a new src/censor_visibility.h header and include it where needed. Or unify: use CENSOR_API everywhere for test-visible internal symbols and reserve CENSOR_EXPORT for the 5 public ABI functions.
